newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed a little lower on Monday after a day dominated by technical factors, with very high futures volume and the December contract on its last day of full trade.

"The Spanish market rose a lot on Friday and also this morning. But later we had technical factors predominating," a dealer said. Trading volume rose because of the roll-over between the two contracts, with December trading 71,811 contracts and closing at 112.10 and the March contract trading 47,517, ending at 111.60. "But the underlying trend in the domestic market is still very positive," a dealer added.
"Tomorrow the opening will depend on the foreign outlook as always but I do expect the market to reach new record highs very soon," he added.

In morning trade, the long-term December contract reached 112.73, just short of the record high at 112.92. The cash 10-year spread over Bunds was closing at 112 basis points, after it hit its record low this morning at 104 basis points.
"The 100 basis points is very strong resistance," one analyst said.
